questions.stem: A vector goes from point A(1, 3) to point B(7, −1). What is the column vector representing AB?
questions.explanation: The column vector AB = B − A = (7−1, −1−3) = (6, −4). Option (b) is the vector BA (going the wrong way). Option (d) forgets to subtract the y-coordinates correctly.

questions.stem: What is the magnitude of the vector (−3, 4)?
questions.explanation: Magnitude = sqrt((-3)² + 4²) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt(25) = 5. Option (b) adds the absolute values. Option (d) forgets to take the square root.

questions.stem: Two vectors are equal if they have the same magnitude and direction. Vector p goes from (0, 0) to (3, 5). Which vector is equal to p?
questions.explanation: Vector p = (3, 5). Option (a): (5−2, 6−1) = (3, 5), which matches. Option (b) gives (−3, −5), the negative of p. Option (c) gives (5, 3), wrong direction. Option (d) gives (3, 4), wrong y-component.

questions.stem: A ship sails on a bearing that can be described by the column vector (5, −12). What distance does the ship travel?
questions.explanation: Distance = magnitude = sqrt(5² + (−12)²) = sqrt(25 + 144) = sqrt(169) = 13 km. Option (a) adds the absolute values. Option (d) forgets the square root.

questions.stem: The vector −a is the negative of vector a. If a = (−2, 7), what is the column vector −a?
questions.explanation: The negative of a vector reverses both components: −(−2, 7) = (2, −7). Option (a) only negates the x-component. Option (b) only negates the y-component.
